title: The 5 Densest Elements on Earth, Ranked (#1 Is Twice as Heavy as Lead)

scenes.text: The five densest elements on Earth, ranked. Number one isn't gold, and it isn't lead.

scenes.label: Gold · 19.3 g/cm³
scenes.text: Number five: gold. A one-liter bottle of it would weigh over nineteen kilograms.

scenes.label: Rhenium · 21 g/cm³
scenes.text: Number four: rhenium, a rare metal in jet engine parts. A liter of it weighs about twenty-one kilograms.

scenes.label: Platinum · 21.5 g/cm³
scenes.text: Number three: platinum. A liter weighs about twenty-one and a half kilograms.

scenes.label: Iridium · 22.56 g/cm³
scenes.text: Number two: iridium. Just a hair lighter than number one, and it barely corrodes.

scenes.label: Osmium · 22.59 g/cm³
scenes.text: Number one: osmium. A liter of it weighs about twenty-two and a half kilograms, twice as dense as lead.

description:
The five densest elements on Earth, ranked.
Gold barely makes the list. The winner, osmium, packs about twice as much weight into the same space as lead.
Which one surprised you most?
first_comment: Did you guess osmium? And what should we rank next?
